title: introduce model intake manifest, deterministic perf fingerprint, and release briefing generator
author: Diego Alvarez
description: Context: Add a first-class model intake manifest plus a deterministic performance fingerprint and an automated release-brief generator. The intake manifest captures vendor metadata, dataset provenance, license, intended use-cases, minimum serving constraints (memory/seq-length), and optional privacy tags. The perf fingerprint is a compact, deterministic summary of latency and token-cost behavior across a small canonical workload (short, medium, long sequences) used for quick compatibility and regression checks. The release briefing generator synthesizes short release notes from manifest diffs and perf-fingerprint deltas so maintainers get a concise rollout blurb during onboarding and version bumps. Motivation: reduce manual churn when onboarding models; enable fast automated regressions checks for Dedicated/Private deployments; produce consistent short-form notes for Console and the model registry UI. What this PR contains: manifest schema (schemas/manifest_v1.json + type bindings), ingestion pipeline to validate and store manifests on model upload, perf fingerprint extractor (deterministic runner using canned seeds and telemetry hooks), brief-generator (templates + delta heuristics), a CLI tool for maintainers (tools/manifestctl) and a backfill script to seed manifests for ~200 recent models. Migration: new DB table model_manifests and perf_fingerprints; backfill executed as a one-time migration under feature flag. Rollout plan: opt-in feature flag model_intake_manifest_v1 -> staged backfill on low-traffic hours -> surface brief in Console -> enable CI hook that blocks PRs without manifest for new-model uploads. Rollback: disable feature flag and revert migration script; manifests are additive so no data-loss expected. Checklist: [x] manifest schema and type bindings, [x] fingerprint extractor implementation, [x] brief generator + templates, [x] CLI and backfill script, [x] unit + e2e tests, [x] docs and examples. Related work: ENG-7281 (registry onboarding improvements), PM-1049 (release note automation). Notes: this does not change public SDK APIs; registry internal endpoints involved are behind the feature flag. See docs/registry/manifest.md for full schema and examples.
commits: 1) Add manifest_v1 schema and TypeScript bindings; 2) Implement perf fingerprint extractor and deterministic runner; 3) Add brief-generator and templates; 4) CLI tool manifestctl + backfill script; 5) DB migration for manifests and fingerprints; 6) Tests, docs and examples; 7) Fix: handle missing license field gracefully (follow-up after reviewer feedback).

release_notes: Introduce model intake manifest v1, deterministic perf fingerprints for fast regression checks, and a release briefing generator that auto-synthesizes short release notes from manifest and perf deltas. Backfill provided for recent models. Feature gated behind model_intake_manifest_v1.
notes_for_ops: DB migration creates table model_manifests and perf_fingerprints; backfill script is idempotent and uses advisory locks. Run backfill during low-traffic window. Feature flag controls UI and CI behaviour.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for schema validation, extractor determinism, and brief generator templates. E2E backfill test added. CI runs included linters, unit tests, and a dedicated e2e job for manifest backfill that was retried once due to a DB race.
security_considerations: Manifest allows optional sensitive tags; UI redacts fields labelled as 'sensitive' by default. Backfill respects vendor-supplied redaction markers. No new network endpoints are public; all changes are internal to registry behind feature flag.
qa_steps: 1) Run tools/manifestctl against local registry with sample examples/model_with_manifest.yaml; 2) Validate perf_fingerprint produced matches tests/unit golden files; 3) Trigger brief generation on a manifest diff and confirm output length <= 280 chars for Console summary; 4) Run backfill script in staging and verify no duplicate manifests created.
notes: This PR started as an internal effort to reduce manual release note writing for model upgrades; the brief-generator uses a small template engine and conservative heuristics to avoid misleading claims about model behavior. We will iterate the brevity heuristics after initial rollouts based on PM feedback.
